title: T1041 — Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Exfiltration Over C2 Channel with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Quiet beacon
steps.caption: The implant on ENG-WS-14 beacons to its C2 server over HTTPS every 60 seconds. Each check-in is a few hundred bytes - a heartbeat, nothing more. baseline shows a tiny, regular channel - 60-second interval, about 300 B per POST
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Operator sends a task
steps.caption: Through the same channel, the operator tasks the implant: grab documents from the engineering file share. the beacon reply is unusually long this time - task delivery rides the same HTTPS session
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Files are read and encoded
steps.caption: The implant reads documents from the file server and base64-encodes them, turning any file into text that fits inside ordinary web traffic. Sysmon (a Windows add-on that logs process and network events) shows many document file reads and no archiver spawned - the encoder lives inside the implant itself
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Data rides the same channel
steps.caption: The implant streams the encoded files back inside task replies: 48 POSTs of 512 KB, same domain, same TLS pattern (TLS is the encryption that HTTPS uses). client-to-server bytes on the beacon channel hit 1000x baseline; no new domain appears anywhere
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: C2 reassembles the data
steps.caption: On the attacker side, the chunks become the original files again. From the network, nothing new is visible - the theft is complete. only the same beacon destination. Without volume analytics, this step is invisible
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: The rhythm gives it away
steps.caption: The 60-second interval never changes; only the size does. periodicity unchanged, volume up 1000x, and the upload-to-download ratio flips to 85:1
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Analytics compare with baseline
steps.caption: The SOC checks the destination against 90 days of history: rare for this subnet, abnormal byte ratio - the exact shape ATT&CK calls AN0990. rare-destination first-seen plus bad ratio - two weak signals that agree become one strong case
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Contain the channel
steps.caption: The SOC sinkholes the C2 domain - it takes over the name so the beacon can no longer resolve - and isolates ENG-WS-14. The pipe that carried the data out now leads nowhere. containment confirmed; the estate-wide hunt for the same beacon shape begins
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.
